expected_text_segments:
September PPI: energy drove the goods surge as services rose

Why it matters: In the September 2026 release, BLS attributed over 80% of the goods increase to energy, which rose 10.8%. Services prices also rose 0.8%.

Context: The September 2026 countercase is concentration: goods excluding foods and energy rose 0.3%, and services excluding trade, transportation and warehousing also rose 0.3%.

Read the full brief: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/september-ppi-energy-drove-the-goods

Retrospective analysis, written on 5 November 2026 (GMT+7) Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade.

media_manifest.alt_text: Two years of first-reported monthly PPI changes; September headline 1.3%, underlying 0.5%.
media_manifest.attribution: BLS dated first releases; monthly change, seasonally adjusted; October 2024-September 2026. Each point retains its original dated-release source.
media_manifest.caption: October 2024–September 2026. Each month retains its dated first release. Underlying excludes foods, energy and trade services; later revisions are not substituted. Sources: [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CC-010 first-print projection) · 15 Oct 2026](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm); [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CC-010 first-print projection) · 15 Oct 2026](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm).
media_manifest.placement_after: How September compares with two years of first releases

media_manifest.alt_text: September PPI: final demand 1.3%, goods 2.6%, services 0.8%, excluding foods, energy and trade services 0.5%.
media_manifest.attribution: BLS, September 2026 PPI, 15 October 2026 release; monthly SA changes. Rates, not contributions.
media_manifest.caption: Separate monthly rates, not percentage-point contributions. The underlying measure overlaps goods and services; the bars do not add to the headline. Sources: [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm).
media_manifest.placement_after: September's jump was broad, but uneven

steps: name_session; list tabs, open a task-owned tab
snapshot; verify current signed-in publishing identity exactly; login is an owner action
bind exact approved payload/media and reconciled canonical URL; use snapshot refs only
PUBLISH or EDIT_EXISTING only under this sole-coordinator authorization; READBACK never submits or retries
read back stable public object ID, exact public URL, identity and content; preserve ambiguity
request.substack_media_readback: Return public_image_urls observed on the exact canonical page; the existing media owner verifies original bytes before derivative delivery.

browser_workspace.window: Use the one existing BrowserOS Neo window. Create one only if none exists.
browser_workspace.tabs: Open tabs with tabs action=new and groupId in this task's group, titled Capital Chronicle/<task>. Leave Jim's and other agents' tabs untouched.

composed_run.one_run: One BrowserOS Neo run script does all three steps in this order, in this task's tab.

1_identity.rule: Read the signed-in account and compare it with the expected identity and stable id. While in this identity or any other pre-write part, result.stage is BEFORE_PUBLISH_CLICK. A mismatch or an unreadable identity returns FAILED_BEFORE_WRITE with definite_no_write true, stage BEFORE_PUBLISH_CLICK and no click.

composed_run.2_publish: Immediately BEFORE the publish click, set the observation's dispatched_at_utc and result.stage = PUBLISH_CLICK_ATTEMPTED; then click once to publish the exact payload.
composed_run.3_readback: Read back the published object (id, url, text, media) in the same run.

return.result: the publish result, as for any PUBLISH step, with its stage

composed.readback: the READBACK result fields, observed after the publish

composed_run.after_click: FAILED_BEFORE_WRITE is a definite no-write only for an account mismatch or stage BEFORE_PUBLISH_CLICK. Any other failure, including a missing stage, is UNKNOWN_WRITE; the coordinator reads back before any retry.
